catalog_quote: [p. 164] The stress systems are also very similar at the word level, with stress generally falling on the last syllable in nouns and adjectives but having a tendency towards the initial position in verbs. [p. 171] ... most notably the prefix /bæ/ that appears behind perfective, subjunctive, and imperative verbs. ... Mazandarani (like most — perhaps all — Iranian languages) does not have secondary stress. Thus, there is hardly any motivation to assume binary feet of any kind for this language (but see Rahmani 2019 for an attempt to attribute binary feet independent of stress to Persian words). Focusing on main stress alone, we observe that the stress pattern is not related to the vowel alternation in any meaningful way. In all of the verbs we examined, the stress is on the preverb; yet raising targets the preverb in some cases and the stem in others. [p. 178] This may be due to the fact that the first syllable is stressed in prefixed verbs. [Mokhtarian 2005: 15, §6.4] Das Präteritum wird meist durch die Präfixe /ba-/, /da-/, /de-/, /ha-/ und /hā-/ + Präteritalstamm + Personalendung gebildet. Das Präfix zieht hierbei den Wortakzent auf sich. [Mokhtarian 2005: 10-11, §3.1] Der Plural wird regelhaft mit den Suffixen -(h)ā und -un gebildet, welche dem Nomen angefügt werden und nicht die Betonung auf sich ziehen.

new_statements.rule_in_words: Persian-type part-of-speech-conditioned word stress: in nouns and adjectives primary stress falls on the final syllable of the word; in verbs it tends to the initial syllable, specifically the preverb/prefix (ba-, da-, de-, ha-, hā-) in prefixed verb forms (confirmed independently by Mokhtarian 2005: 15, 'Das Präfix zieht hierbei den Wortakzent auf sich'). No secondary stress.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Explicitly denied: 'Mazandarani (like most — perhaps all — Iranian languages) does not have secondary stress' (p. 171).
new_statements.exceptions: Verbs: stress on the preverb/initial syllable rather than final (pp. 164, 171, 178). Mokhtarian 2005 (Tübingen dissertation, pp. 10-17) adds that plural -(h)ā/-un, definite-object -e, attributive -e and indirect-object -ra are unstressed (so stress stays on the stem-final syllable), while substantivizing -i and the infinitive ending -(j)en are stressed and preterite prefixes attract the word accent. The p. 164 statement is hedged with 'generally' and is a comparison with Persian, not an exhaustive rule.
new_statements.domain_note: Word level ('at the word level'); citation/elicited forms from native speakers of the Amol, Babol and Reineh dialects. The article's topic is vowel dissimilation, so the stress statement is brief background, not a dedicated prosodic analysis.
new_statements.identity_note: Mahdavi Mazdeh & Nehzati 2024 describe the dialects of Amol, Babol and Reineh (Larijan, south of Amol) in central Mazandaran, all within Glottolog's single language maza1291; Mokhtarian 2005 sketches 'the present-day Mazandarani dialect' without naming a locality. The earlier scan's named sources (Yoshie 1996, Nawata 1984) concern the Sari dialect, also maza1291. Glottolog's other refs Borjian 2012 (Velātru/Gachsar) and 2013 (Yushij) describe Caspian-Persian transition-zone varieties in the Alborz, not the core language.

new_statements.translation: [pp. 10-11, §3.1] The plural is formed regularly with the suffixes -(h)ā and -un, which are attached to the noun and do not attract the stress. [p. 11, §3.2] The definite direct object receives a suffix /-e/, which does not attract the stress [...] The indirect object is formed with the unstressed suffix /-ra/. [p. 15, §6.4] The preterite is mostly formed with the prefixes /ba-/, /da-/, /de-/, /ha-/ and /hā-/ + preterite stem + personal ending. The prefix here attracts the word accent. [p. 17, §6.4.7] The infinitive is formed from the preterite stem and the stressed ending /-(j)en/: /da-ket-en/ 'to fall'

new_statements.relation_note: Compatible with the existing statement (Mahdavi Mazdeh & Nehzati 2024: stress final in nouns/adjectives, on the preverb/first syllable in prefixed verbs, no secondary stress) and adds morpheme-level detail: which nominal suffixes are unstressed (plural, object, attributive), which suffixes are stressed (nominalizing -i, infinitive -(j)en, subjunctive endings), and that the preterite prefix bears the word accent. It never states a general rule, so it cannot independently confirm 'final' for underived nouns. The catalog record itself has an empty rule field; this work does not fill it.
new_statements.rule_in_words: The sketch states no general placement rule and has no stress/accent section; stress is mentioned only as a property of individual morphemes. Taken together: nominal inflectional suffixes (plural -(h)ā/-un, definite-object -e, attributive -e, indirect-object -ra) are unstressed, so stress stays on the stem; derivational nominalizing -i (p. 14: 'Durch das betonte Suffixmorphem /-i/ erfolgt die Substantivierung der Adjektive') and the infinitive ending -(j)en are stressed (final); in finite preterite (and imperative/subjunctive-type prefixed) verbs the prefix ba-/da-/de-/ha-/hā- carries the word accent (initial). The 'fixed: final syllable' label is my inference from these morpheme statements, not a rule the author states; confidence low.
new_statements.exceptions: Verbal prefixes take the word accent in the preterite (p. 15); the infinitive ending -(j)en is stressed even in prefixed infinitives (da-ket-én, ba-merd-én, p. 17); p. 22-23 (PDF 25-26), in the medieval-Tabari section: 'Aufgrund der Fehlens diakritischer Vokalzeichen, lässt sich in der HS nicht zwischen Indikativ- und Konjunktivendungen unterscheiden. In Māz sind diese Affixe betont.' (in modern Mazandarani the subjunctive personal endings are stressed). Also p. 10 §2.1: vowels /i, e, o, u/ are long in monosyllables and in the stressed syllable of polysyllables (stress conditions vowel length).
new_statements.identity_note: The dissertation's main body is a philological edition of a medieval Tabari (Old Mazandarani) translation of al-Harīrī's Maqāmāt (ms. Malek 2487); the stress remarks quoted come from the prefatory 'Kurze Beschreibung der heutigen māzandarānischen Mundart' (pp. 7-17), which describes the modern spoken Mazandarani dialect without naming a specific locality in the pages read. The remark on pp. 22-23 contrasts the manuscript's Tabari with modern 'Māz'. The Glottolog open_url (w210.ub.uni-tuebingen.de) no longer resolves (automated download rc 6); the same PDF (1,014,409 bytes) is served athttps://publikationen.uni-tuebingen.de/xmlui/bitstream/handle/10900/46247/pdf/Maqamat_i_Hariri_%28tabarische_Mundart%29.pdf(HTTP 200 verified).

sources.citation: Ivanov, Vladimir B. & Liubov G. Silanteva. 2023. Research on word stress in Iranian languages by Soviet and Russian scholars. Russian Journal of Linguistics 27(2): 392-417. doi:10.22363/2687-0088-31015.
sources.note: Reports the first author's 2014 instrumental study (3 speakers, 34 disyllables, 8 parameters): Mazandarani word stress, previously called dynamic, is 'tonal', i.e. F0 is the main cue of the stressed syllable (mean pitch rise 13%, F0-area also significant); an intonational 'incompleteness' rise on the last syllable of the subject phrase lengthens that unstressed syllable 2-3x; conclusion classes Mazandarani with Persian and Tajik as 'tonal stress (pitch accent, based on F0)'. 'Tonal/pitch accent' here is an acoustic-correlate typology of culminative word stress, not a claim of lexical tone con…

tone.quote: [p. 402] Three native speakers pronounced 34 two-syllable words (68 syllables); 8 parameters of each syllable were analyzed. Previously Mazandarani word stress was described as dynamic, while it was found to be tonal11, i.e., pitch plays the main role in marking the stressed syllable (Sig<0.001). The mean rise of pitch in the stressed syllable equals 13%. […] Mazandarani intonation affects word stress. There is an intonational construction of incompleteness that is very similar to Persian. [p. 412] 1. Tonal stress (pitch accent, based on F0) can be found in Mazandarani (Ivanov 2014), Persian (Ivanov 1972, 1996, Polyakov 1988, Silanteva 2022), and Tajik (Khaskashev 1972, 1983).

tone.quote: 2.1.2. Ударение динамическое, связанное. Падает, как правило, на последний слог слова […]. Не принимают на себя ударения: 1) падежные окончания […]; 2) показатель атрибутивно-качественной формы существительных и прилагательных -е […]. У глаголов в прошедшем длительном времени ударение сохраняется на последнем слоге основы […]; в формах, имеющих префикс ba- (прошедшее нейтральное, настояще-будущее время сослагательного наклонения, перфективная форма сослагательного наклонения, повелительное наклонение), ударение падает на префикс […]. В отрицательных формах глагола ударение падает на частицу отрицания
tone.translation: 2.1.2. Stress is dynamic, bound. As a rule it falls on the last syllable of the word [...]. The following do not take stress: 1) case endings [...]; 2) the marker -e of the attributive-qualitative form of nouns and adjectives [...]. In past-continuous verbs the stress stays on the last syllable of the stem [...]; in forms with the prefix ba- (neutral past, present-future subjunctive, perfective subjunctive, imperative) the stress falls on the prefix [...]. In negative verb forms the stress falls on the negative particle.
